deferredForEditableCoding.adjacentGuideText:
### Review: what does self-custody responsibility mean?

<!-- VISUAL: BD-V-052
ALT: Self-custody responsibility map connecting key control, verification, backups, errors, and support.
ASSET: y_assets (archived)/diploma/bd-v-052.svg
-->

<!-- VISUAL: BD-V-053
ALT: Text-equivalent summary of self-custody responsibilities and safe decision points.
ASSET: y_assets (archived)/diploma/bd-v-053.svg
-->

Imagine that a friend sends you a payment request while an unfamiliar support account says you must act immediately. What could you check before doing anything? Can you protect a recovery plan, distinguish receiving information from secrets, and verify the person, payment method, destination, amount, and final screen before sending? Whether a service or you control the keys, the practical recap is the same: protect secrets, verify before approving, recognize scam signals, and keep mistakes small while learning.

deferredConnectors: Eight responsibility spokes connect to control of keys, with no ranking.
deferredLabels: Backup — protect usable private recovery information; losing it can prevent recovery.
Recovery — check compatibility and method privately; wrong method can fail.
Receiving — verify method, network and request; mismatches may prevent receipt.
Sending — verify destination, amount and final summary; valid sends are usually irreversible.
Tool choice — verify source and responsibilities; unsafe tools can expose funds or secrets.
Acquisition path — check full route; fees, custody and settlement can differ.
Privacy — protect personal information; public activity can be linked.
Scam checks — stop and verify independently; sharing secrets can lose control.
